items.stem: A storage room is a cuboid 15 m long, 14 m wide and 2 m high. Find the length of the space diagonal and the angle it makes with the base, to 3 s.f.
items.markingKey: Base diagonal √(15² + 14²) = 20.52 (M1 A1); space diagonal 20.6 (A1); tan θ = 2/20.52, θ = 5.57° (A1).

items.stem: In triangle PQR, angle P = 85°, angle Q = 77° and the side opposite P is 8 cm. Find the other two sides to 3 s.f.
items.answer: side opposite Q: 7.82 cm; side opposite R: 2.48 cm
items.markingKey: Third angle 18° (A1); sine rule 8/sin 85° = x/sin 77° (M1); 7.82 (A1); 2.48 (A1).

items.stem: Two ferries leave the port of Auckland at the same time. One sails at 13 km/h and the other at 21 km/h, on courses 129° apart. (a) Find how far each has sailed after 3 hours. (b) State the angle between their paths. (c) Find the distance between them. (d) Describe how the distance between them changes over time.
items.answer: (a) 39 km and 63 km (b) 129° (c) 92.6 km (d) the distance grows by 30.9 km each hour
items.markingKey: (a) 39 km and 63 km (b) 129° (c) 92.6 km (d) the distance grows by 30.9 km each hour. Cosine rule set up (M1 A1); results accurate (A1); interpreted in context (D: R1); clear communication with units (C1).

items.stem: Investigate 45°, 135°, 225° and 315°. (a) Find the exact sine of each. (b) Find the exact cosine of each. (c) Describe the pattern. (d) State a rule for which ratios are positive in each quadrant.
items.answer: (a) sin: √2/2, √2/2, −√2/2, −√2/2 (b) cos: √2/2, −√2/2, −√2/2, √2/2 (c) the values repeat with sign changes by quadrant (d) "All Students Take Calculus": all, sin, tan, cos positive in quadrants 1–4
items.markingKey: (a) sin: √2/2, √2/2, −√2/2, −√2/2 (b) cos: √2/2, −√2/2, −√2/2, √2/2 (c) the values repeat with sign changes by quadrant (d) "All Students Take Calculus": all, sin, tan, cos positive in quadrants 1–4. Unit-circle values (A1 A1); quadrant / sign reasoning (R1); pattern or context (B/D: R1); communication (C1).

items.stem: A logo in London is cut from a circle of radius 16 cm by a chord that subtends 60° at the centre. (a) Find the area of the sector. (b) Find the area of the triangle formed by the chord and the radii. (c) Find the area of the segment. (d) Express the segment as a percentage of the circle.
items.answer: (a) 134.0 cm² (b) 110.9 cm² (c) 23.2 cm² (d) 2.88% of the circle
items.markingKey: (a) 134.0 cm² (b) 110.9 cm² (c) 23.2 cm² (d) 2.88% of the circle. ½ab sin C applied (M1 A1); composite area organised (A1); context / exact value (D: R1); communication (C1).

items.stem: A hiker near Dubai sees the summit of a hill at an angle of elevation of 10°. After walking 669 m directly towards it on level ground, the angle is 27°. (a) Find the angle at the summit in the triangle formed. (b) Find the distance from the second point to the summit. (c) Find the height of the hill. (d) Find the remaining horizontal distance to the point below the summit.
items.answer: (a) 17° (b) 397 m (c) 180 m (d) horizontal distance from the second point 354 m
items.markingKey: (a) 17° (b) 397 m (c) 180 m (d) horizontal distance from the second point 354 m. Diagram / angles correctly identified (A1); sine or cosine rule and Pythagoras applied (M1 A1); bearings in three-figure form (C1); interpretation (D: R1).

items.stem: The ambiguous case can occur when you know:
options: three angles
two angles and a side
three sides
two sides and a non-included angle
items.answer: two sides and a non-included angle
items.markingKey: D. SSA.

items.stem: Which term matches this description: "The rearranged formula cos A = (b² + c² − a²)/(2bc)"?
options: back bearing
unit circle
area formula ½ab sin C
cosine rule for angles
items.answer: cosine rule for angles
items.markingKey: D. This is the definition of cosine rule for angles.

items.stem: sin 150° equals:
options: −cos 30°
cos 30°
sin 30°
−sin 30°
items.answer: sin 30°
items.markingKey: C. sin(180° − θ) = sin θ.

items.stem: Explain why ½ab sin C gives ½ab for a right angle.
items.answer: sin 90° = 1, so it reduces to ½ × base × height.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: sin 90° = 1, so it reduces to ½ × base × height. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Explain why a navigator writes 050° rather than 50° for a bearing.
items.answer: Bearings use three figures so that every direction has a standard, unambiguous form from 000° to 359°.
items.markingKey: Three figures (R1); reason (R1).

items.stem: In triangle ABC, A = 31°, a = 6 cm and b = 11 cm. Ingrid finds B = 70.8° and stops. Explain why there may be another triangle.
items.answer: sin B = 0.944 is also satisfied by B = 109.2°; since 31° + 109.2° < 180°, a second triangle exists.
items.markingKey: Supplementary angle (R1); check of angle sum (A1).

items.stem: Sofia calculates a² = 11² + 11² − 2(11)(11) cos 100° and says the answer must be smaller than 11² + 11² = 242. Explain the mistake.
items.answer: cos 100° is negative, so −2bc cos A is positive and a² = 284.0 is larger than 242.
items.markingKey: Sign of cos (R1); value (A1).

items.stem: Explain why sin²θ + cos²θ = 1.
items.answer: The point (cos θ, sin θ) is on the unit circle; by Pythagoras its coordinates satisfy x² + y² = 1.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: The point (cos θ, sin θ) is on the unit circle; by Pythagoras its coordinates satisfy x² + y² = 1. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: "If the area and two sides are known, the included angle is unique." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: sin C = k has two solutions C and 180° − C.
items.markingKey: sin C = k has two solutions C and 180° − C. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: A yacht leaves a harbour near Busan and sails 27 km on a bearing of 200°, then 36 km on a bearing of 040°. Find its distance from the harbour and the bearing it must sail to return.
items.answer: 14.1 km; bearing 261°
items.markingKey: Angle in the triangle 20° (M1); cosine rule 14.1 km (A1); bearing of the yacht from the harbour 081° (A1); return bearing 261° (A1).

items.stem: In triangle ABC, a = 19 cm, b = 21.9 cm and A = 55°. Find the possible values of angle B, to 1 d.p.
A triangle has sides 13 cm, 19 cm and 20 cm. Find its largest angle to 1 d.p. and state whether the triangle is acute, right-angled or obtuse.
items.answer: 74.7°; acute

items.stem: θ is an obtuse angle with sin θ = 3/5. Find the exact values of cos θ and tan θ.
items.answer: cos θ = −4/5; tan θ = −3/4
items.markingKey: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 (M1); cos²θ = 16/25 (A1); sign from the quadrant (R1); tan θ = sin θ/cos θ (A1).

items.stem: A triangle has area 68.8 cm² and two sides 20 cm and 12 cm. Find the two possible values of the included angle, to 1 d.p.
"The bearing of A from B equals the bearing of B from A." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: They differ by 180°.
items.markingKey: They differ by 180°. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: A student claims: "The sine rule only works in right-angled triangles." Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: It works in any triangle; SOHCAHTOA is the special right-angled case.
items.markingKey: It works in any triangle; SOHCAHTOA is the special right-angled case. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: The roof truss of a house in Sydney is a triangle with base 6 m and rafters 3.9 m and 3.5 m. (a) Find the angle at the top. (b) Is it acute or obtuse? (c) Find the height of the top above the base. (d) Explain a condition the rafter lengths must satisfy.
items.answer: (a) 108.2° (b) obtuse (c) height ≈ 2.16 m (d) the rafters must fit the span: 3.9 + 3.5 > 6
